page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core tests ranking in the top tier (top 10%) and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance in the top 25%. However, multi-core and multi-threaded capabilities are more limited, with stress-ng multi-core performance falling into the average category and Geekbench multi-core scores ranking in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is mixed, showing average speeds for large blocks but weak performance for small cached blocks. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, with web serving falling into the bottom 10%.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs and strong single-core execution, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated compute resources without massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, and lightweight application hosting. However, it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput web serving, or highly parallelized multi-threaded applications due to its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lower multi-core benchmark results.
